ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A solution of carbonic acid, $H_2CO_3$, is titrated with sodium hydroxide, NaOH. The following graph is produced. In addition to $OH^-$, what species are present in the solution during section III of the graph?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The graph shows pH versus volume of NaOH added. The titration curve has labeled sections I through V. Section III is a nearly flat, buffer-like plateau around pH 7–8, located after the first sharp rise near about 10 mL NaOH and before the second sharp rise near about 23 mL NaOH. Reasoning: The acid being titrated is carbonic acid, H2CO3, which is diprotic. After the first proton has been neutralized, the main acid-base pair in solution is bicarbonate and carbonate: HCO3- ⇌ H+ + CO3^2-. Thus, during section III, the relevant species present in addition to OH- are HCO3- and CO3^2-.
